name: American Conservatism
summary: American conservatism is the right-of-centre tradition of the United States, tied since the 1950s to the Republican Party. It combines limited constitutional government, free enterprise and low taxes, traditional moral and religious order, a strong national defence, and patriotism, with factions (traditionalist, libertarian, neoconservative, religious right, populist and national conservative) weighting these differently.
scope: The mainstream post-war fusionist movement (Kirk, Buckley, Goldwater, Reagan) as carried into today's Republican-aligned conservatism, including the Trump-era turn toward tariffs, immigration restriction and national conservatism, drawing on Kirk's ten principles, Goldwater's The Conscience of a Conservative and the 2024 Republican platform. It excludes the libertarian fringe, white-nationalist and neo-Confederate offshoots, and European or British conservatism.

keyFigures.name: Russell Kirk
keyFigures.role: Author of The Conservative Mind (1953) and its ten principles, a founder of traditionalist conservatism.

keyFigures.name: Barry Goldwater
keyFigures.role: Author of The Conscience of a Conservative and 1964 Republican nominee who made limited-government conservatism a national force.

keyFigures.name: Ronald Reagan
keyFigures.role: President whose coalition of social, fiscal and anti-communist conservatives is the model of fusionism.

sources.usedFor: History, factions, fusionism, and typical positions on economy, guns, abortion, immigration, foreign policy and religion.

sources.title: Ten Conservative Principles
sources.author: Russell Kirk (Kirk Center)
sources.usedFor: Traditionalist core: moral order, custom, prudence, variety, property, local community, restraints on power.

sources.title: The Conscience of a Conservative
sources.author: Barry Goldwater
sources.usedFor: Limited government, states' rights, welfare, taxes, unions, farm policy, education, anti-communism, UN and nuclear policy.

sources.title: 2024 Republican Party Platform
sources.author: Republican National Committee (American Presidency Project)
sources.usedFor: Current party positions on taxes, tariffs, immigration, energy, guns, schooling, gender, religion and defence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 2024 platform answers on health care with choice, competition and price transparency rather than a government-provided system; the movement treats a single national provider as a step toward socialism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour market-set wages and the platform is silent on a minimum wage; Goldwater-style limited-government thinking opposes federal wage-setting, though some populist conservatives now accept increases.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Goldwater argues that production is best controlled by the natural operation of the free market, and the fiscal-conservative leg of the movement is defined by deregulation and market primacy.

public-ownership.rationale: Goldwater treats nationalization and welfarism as roads to socialism, and the platform pledges to slash regulation and promote private energy production.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Goldwater defended a flat share of wealth and called graduated rates confiscatory; the 2024 platform makes the 2017 tax cuts permanent and promises further cuts.

unions-good.rationale: Goldwater supports voluntary unionism and right-to-work laws and attacks the concentrated power of union leaders, though recent populist conservatism courts union members.

property-fundamental.rationale: Kirk's seventh principle ties property to freedom and civilization, and Goldwater treats property and earnings as a natural right that government may not lightly infringe.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Conservatives favour deregulation, and the platform promises to slash regulations that stifle jobs, although the populist wing now criticises big technology firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Goldwater says welfarism fosters dependence and erodes character and favours private charity; the 2024 platform however protects Social Security and Medicare, so the claim is stated about welfare programmes broadly rather than entitlements.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership of firms conflicts with Kirk's defence of private property and Goldwater's opposition to socialism; voluntary employee ownership schemes are tolerated but not demanded.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The security-minded mainstream and its anti-communist, law-and-order tradition has generally backed counter-terror surveillance, though libertarian-leaning members dissent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The platform promises to demolish drug cartels and blockade fentanyl, and social conservatives oppose legal recreational drugs, though libertarian conservatives dissent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The platform pledges to ban government collusion in censoring lawful speech, and conservatives generally oppose hate-speech laws as incompatible with the First Amendment.

strong-leader.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater stress restraints on power and separated powers, while the Trump-era populist wing admires a strong executive, so adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: Conservatives treat government as necessary for order; Kirk's ninth principle warns of both anarchy and tyranny, and Goldwater wants limited, not absent, government.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform lists the right to keep and bear arms among its core promises, and the Wikipedia survey notes conservatives generally strongly support gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform promises to replenish police departments, protect officers from frivolous lawsuits and build the strongest military, and Goldwater demanded military superiority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social conservatives uphold traditional moral order, which Kirk calls an enduring moral order, so legalised prostitution is generally opposed.

decide-locally.rationale: Kirk's eighth principle favours local, voluntary decisions and Goldwater defends states' rights and the Tenth Amendment, though conservatives accept national action on defence and borders.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform's emphasis is on locking up violent offenders and law and order; conservatives favour punishment and deterrence though many back reentry programmes.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia describes familialism and family values as core principles, and the platform promotes the sanctity of marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social conservatives oppose same-sex marriage and the platform promotes the sanctity of marriage, but acceptance has grown within the movement and the issue is now treated as settled by many.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anti-abortion stands are a listed principle of the movement; the 2024 platform shifted to leaving the matter to the states and opposing late-term abortion, so the typical adherent still opposes broad legality.

more-religion-public.rationale: Goldwater places spiritual ends above material ones and the Christian right seeks laws reflecting Christian morality; the platform proposes a task force against anti-Christian bias.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Conservatives favour colour-blind law and Goldwater held that civil rights come from law not remedial programmes; the platform opposes race-based discrimination in schools.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The platform moves to keep men out of women's sports and reverse Title IX changes, consistent with the traditionalist view that human nature is constant.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kirk's principles of custom, convention and continuity, and the patriotism listed as a core principle, make preserving national tradition central.

gradual-change.rationale: Kirk's fourth and tenth principles state that reform must be deliberate and change gradual, with prudence guiding it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The platform promises mass deportation and ending chain migration, and national conservatives favour restriction, though the free-market leg has historically favoured high legal immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Goldwater warns against surrendering sovereignty to the UN, and Wikipedia notes national conservatives are sceptical of the UN and globalism.

free-trade.rationale: Fusionist conservatives long championed free trade but the platform now backs baseline tariffs, so a typical adherent today is genuinely split.

nation-first.rationale: The platform's America-first framing and the sovereignty emphasis of national conservatism favour national interests, though the internationalist, alliance-building strand dissents.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Neoconservatives favour intervention but paleo- and national conservatives are non-interventionist, and Goldwater justified foreign action by national interest rather than human rights.

open-borders.rationale: The platform calls for completing the border wall and deporting illegal migrants, and every conservative strand rejects open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The platform promises to unleash American energy and end the Green New Deal; the movement regards growth as the basis of prosperity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wikipedia notes American conservatives are more likely to question anthropogenic climate change, and the platform rejects the Green New Deal.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kirk's imperfectability principle warns against utopian faith in progress, while the market-optimist leg is more upbeat; this is inferred from principles.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The platform backs energy from all sources including nuclear, and the pro-energy conservative mainstream supports expansion.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kirk warns that hasty sweeping change creates new abuses, though the American conservative tradition honours the Revolution as a restoration of rights.

experts-over-public.rationale: Conservatives are generally sceptical of credentialed elites and the populist wing especially so, while Kirk favours a natural aristocracy of character rather than expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Goldwater argues that production is best left to free markets and that planning leads toward socialism; Kirk opposes economic leveling.

socialized-markets.rationale: Workers' or public ownership of all firms conflicts with the private-property emphasis, even if markets are used; inferred from Goldwater and Kirk on property.

land-value-tax.rationale: Conservatives want lower taxes, and a single land tax replacing others is a Georgist idea not discussed in the sources, so this is inferred from their general stance on taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The platform's tax-cutting stance and Goldwater's view of property as a right lead conservatives to oppose heavy inheritance taxes, the estate tax being a classic target.

basic-income.rationale: Goldwater argues welfarism creates dependence and favours private charity, and unconditional state income cuts against that; inferred from the sources' welfare position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The 2024 platform promises baseline tariffs and Buy American policies, and protectionism has grown more prominent among conservatives, though the older fusionist wing dissents.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Goldwater and the fiscal wing oppose state direction of the economy, although some national conservatives now back industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Kirk sees property as the foundation of independence and variety, which suggests broad ownership is welcome, but conservatives defend corporate property too; the sources do not discuss concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wage labour is a communist aim contrary to Kirk's defence of property and Goldwater's free-market stance.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some libertarian-conservatives want to end the Fed, but the mainstream accepts a central bank; the sources do not address it, so this is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices contradict Goldwater's opposition to industry-wide bargaining power and to state economic control.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kirk's ninth principle demands limits on power, and Goldwater defines the Constitution as a system of restraints, which rules out single-party ideological rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kirk honours Burkean tradition, but American conservatism is republican in origin and rarely discusses monarchy; adherents are indifferent.

democracy-best.rationale: American conservatives defend constitutional republican government, but with scepticism of majority rule and talk of republic rather than democracy, so the answer is qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater favour representative, constitutionally limited government over plebiscites; some western conservatives back ballot initiatives.

workers-councils.rationale: Council government is never discussed by Kirk, Goldwater or the platform; rejection is inferred from their defence of the constitutional order.

right-to-secede.rationale: Goldwater defends states' rights but within the Union; most conservatives reject a legal right of secession, though a minority of paleoconservatives dissent.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kirk's fifth principle defends natural distinctions and hierarchies of class and condition, and the movement's tradition speaks of a natural aristocracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Conservatives condemn political violence in general but honour the American Revolution and self-defence; this is inferred and adherents are split on wording.

war-builds-character.rationale: Goldwater stresses sacrifice and victory but the sources never say war builds character; adherents are divided and this is inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Christian right seeks laws reflecting Christian morality, and the platform backs religious liberty over strict separation, though most accept non-establishment.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The religious right wants laws consistent with Christian morality but most conservatives do not seek laws derived directly from scripture; Goldwater appeals to the laws of God and nature.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Goldwater limits government to defence, justice and property protection, meaning the state provides those; only the libertarian fringe privatises them.

military-superiority.rationale: Goldwater states that mere parity will not do and the platform pledges the strongest and most powerful military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Conservatives define the nation by constitutional culture rather than ethnicity, although a paleoconservative strand and Huntington-style arguments lean toward cultural homogeneity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kirk's principles defend class variety and reject leveling, and Goldwater regards class-conflict theory as the socialist view of society.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kirk's fifth principle states that forced equalisation leads to stagnation or new tyranny, and Goldwater defends differences earned by individual effort.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; conservatives emphasise national and private property rights, so authority for particular groups is inferred to be disfavoured.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Conservatives oppose reparations in general and the platform has no such provision; this is inferred from the opposition to race-based remedies.

civilizational-union.rationale: American conservatives stress national sovereignty and scepticism of supranational bodies; this is inferred from Goldwater's UN position.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Goldwater stresses individual responsibility for development and market economics; religious conservatives qualify self-interest with duty, so the agreement is moderate.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kirk's prescription and community emphasize duty, but Goldwater's individualism and rights-based constitutionalism cut the other way; adherents are split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist and religious conservatives often affirm created nature's worth while the market wing is instrumental, so it is split.

limit-population.rationale: The platform and pronatalist family emphasis oppose coercive population control; this is inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement is pro-growth and pro-energy, so it rejects the claim that industry has been a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Kirk's prudence and continuity principles caution against disrupting institutions for the sake of change, though market conservatives like innovation.

human-enhancement.rationale: Traditionalist and religious conservatives such as bioconservatives are wary of redesigning human nature; inferred rather than directly sourced.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed, but Kirk's emphasis on prudence and human judgment and wariness of centralised power point against handing governance to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Libertarian conservatives support encryption while law-and-order conservatives want lawful access; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kirk values continuity and the enduring moral order but also prudent improvement, and Goldwater looks forward to freedom; progress is not rejected, yet Kirk accepts neither pure restoration nor progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kirk's prudence stresses consequences, but American conservatives prize principle, as Goldwater's constitutional absolutism shows, so adherents favour principle over pragmatic tests.

direct-action.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater work through elections, constitutional limits and parties, rejecting revolutionary direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a conservative formulation; Kirk's prudence implies caution about means but the sources do not state this prefigurative claim.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Foraging life is never discussed; rejection is inferred from Kirk's defence of civilisation and inherited institutions.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The abolition of the division of labour is a Marxist aim at odds with the market economy and variety that Goldwater and Kirk defend.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Goldwater says earnings are the individual's property and rejects distribution by need as socialism; Kirk rejects economic leveling.

production-for-use.rationale: Conservatives defend profit-based markets, as Goldwater's free-market argument shows, against production planned for use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Goldwater and Kirk defend profit as part of free enterprise and property, rejecting the Marxist exploitation thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Goldwater calls communism a mortal enemy aiming at world domination, and the position is plainly rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: Goldwater argues farm production is best left to the market and individual farmers and Kirk defends private property, which clearly implies rejecting collective farming, though neither discusses it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Conservatives hold that communist expansion, not capitalism, is the cause of war, as Goldwater argues in discussing the Soviet threat.

taxation-theft.rationale: Goldwater treats heavy taxation as a limit on freedom but accepts that government has a right to claim an equal percentage of wealth, so taxation is not itself theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order and social conservatives' morals legislation reject the view that only harm to others justifies restriction, though libertarian conservatives agree.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Goldwater stresses individual rights but Kirk's voluntary communities and the family as an institution suggest group rights matter; split and inferred.

conscription.rationale: Goldwater and the platform stress military strength, but conservatives are split between compulsion and the all-volunteer force; the sources do not say.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Conservatives value both federalism and the vote; this exit-based claim is a libertarian one that is inferred to be disfavoured by most adherents.

state-as-business.rationale: Fiscal conservatives praise business efficiency, but treating citizens as customers who can leave is a libertarian notion; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Goldwater defines freedom as the absence of coercion by government and attacks welfarism, rejecting freedom as material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conservatives often charge that universities and media hold outsized power over elected officials, and the platform opposes federal collusion to censor speech.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a defined mainstream position; most conservatives reject racial hierarchy claims, though a fringe entertains them, so it is inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Kirk's emphasis on families, communities and associations echoes organic representation, but American conservatives work through parties and Congress; split.

total-state.rationale: Goldwater says government represents power over others and Kirk demands limited power, so a state directing every area of life is rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Make America Great Again theme speaks of renewal after decline, though traditionalists would prefer restoration to radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Goldwater called for strength and victory over communism rather than expansion, though recent conservatives voice territorial ambitions at times; majority opposes.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths are never discussed; rejection is inferred from the movement's constitutionalism.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is never discussed; rejection is inferred from Goldwater's and Kirk's defence of property and individual liberty.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order affirms permanent truths, and conservatives attack postmodern relativism in the academy.

universal-morality.rationale: Kirk's first principle holds that moral truths are permanent, and Goldwater says the laws of God and nature have no dateline.

single-common-good.rationale: Kirk's moral order suggests a common good, but Goldwater favours pluralism and individual choice; split and inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The platform pledges to stand with Israel, and Christian Zionism is a listed conservative principle.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the conservative immigration stance disfavours open citizenship claims, though Israel's law of return is supported by many.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not an American conservative issue; adherents are indifferent.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' votes on company management cut against property rights and Goldwater's critique of union power.

school-vouchers.rationale: The platform supports universal school choice and Wikipedia notes conservatives favour vouchers including for religious schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Goldwater says spending cuts should come before tax cuts, and balanced budgets are a fiscal conservative aim, though the 2024 platform offers no deficit target.

economic-freedom.rationale: Goldwater ties political freedom to economic freedom and Kirk's seventh principle links property with freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Conservatives favour law and constitutional rules; Confucian rule by example is not an American conservative idea, so this is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sovereignty and national interest are stressed by the platform and by Goldwater's scepticism of international bodies.

force-without-un.rationale: Goldwater warns against UN control of American policy, and the platform supports American strength without deference to international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater place spiritual and moral truths alongside reason, and religion is central to the movement, so reason alone is not the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The platform's focus on citizens and ending incentives for illegal migration implies welfare reserved for citizens; this is a mainstream conservative position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Goldwater argues welfare erodes character and dependence, and work requirements were the 1990s conservative policy.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kirk's emphasis on variety and harmonious orders and Goldwater's opposition to class warfare lead conservatives to favour cooperation between employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Kirk's continuity and prescription principles and Goldwater's definition of schools as transmitting cultural heritage reject sacrificing inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; a common front against Western powers opposes the conservative alignment with the West, so it is inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives reject class organisation yet favour national over international loyalty, a partial overlap.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatives value distinct family roles but American law has moved to equal treatment; most do not seek legally distinct public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Prohibiting interest contradicts the market economy that conservatives defend; only some religious thinkers favour it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Goldwater held that integration is just though left to the states; modern conservatism rejects legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The idea of the state as the tool of the ruling class is Marxist, and conservatives treat government as an instrument of order and law.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The platform promises to unleash American energy and end limits on oil, gas and coal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The platform emphasises English, Authentic Civics and patriotic education, and national conservatives stress assimilation into the national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some populist conservatives voice replacement claims but the mainstream rejects them; adherents are split.

proportional-representation.rationale: American conservatives support the existing constitutional system of single-member districts and a federal structure, though they do not discuss it.

national-mission.rationale: American exceptionalism is a listed conservative principle, yet paleoconservatives reject spreading the American model; neocons support it, so adherents are split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservatives reject structural patriarchy as a feminist claim and the platform frames policy in terms of keeping men out of women's sports.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist-era conservatives voice distrust of elites, and Goldwater says government concentrates power in some men, but traditionalists defend elected officials.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits conflict with the religious and pro-life conservative view of human dignity.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The platform protects police officers from frivolous lawsuits and favours the military, so legal accountability for past killings is disfavoured.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Goldwater defines government's role in terms of defending the country, enforcing justice and protecting property, though the platform and social conservatives want more than that.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects racial discouragement of marriage and holds equal rights before law.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Goldwater says each man is responsible for his own development and Kirk affirms permanent moral truths, consistent with equal rights before the law, though Kirk defends social variety.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist internal debate that conservatives do not address; they hold socialism fails regardless.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Conservatives defend the legitimacy of the American and Israeli states, and the platform stands with Israel.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal law for all citizens fits Goldwater's constitutionalism, though religious liberty exemptions are also valued; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The platform defends First Amendment religious liberty, so restricting conversion is contrary.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A cattle-slaughter ban is an Indian measure the movement never addressed; rejection is inferred from its defence of property and agriculture.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian conservatives favour school prayer and religious school vouchers, so they oppose strict exclusion of religion.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Soviet state doctrine is never discussed; rejection is inferred from conservative limited-government commitments.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Goldwater affirms constitutional government resting on the Constitution and American political tradition draws on the Declaration, though Kirk grounds authority also in prescription.

trade-surplus.rationale: The platform's tariffs and Buy American stance imply favouring exports, but market conservatives deny mercantilism; split and inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Conservatives oppose forced emigration of minorities, and American deportation policy targets illegal migrants not minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: This is a libertarian axiom; the mainstream accepts state force and Goldwater's victory policy, so they disagree.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Goldwater's free-market argument and Kirk's variety principle favour competition between individuals, though not as struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are divided between First Amendment absolutism and anti-communist restrictions that were once supported.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory not discussed; Goldwater's negative liberty only partly overlaps with it.

separated-powers.rationale: Kirk's ninth principle requires power to be limited and balanced, and Goldwater calls the Constitution a system of restraints.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Leninist vanguard thesis is never discussed; rejection is inferred from Goldwater's anti-communism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Goldwater says welfarism is a danger and Kirk defends variety of conditions; charity is encouraged but laws should not prioritise the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British policy; conservatives favour widespread property ownership, so this is inferred from their property stance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Goldwater favours right-to-work and restraining union political power, and wants union leaders subject to law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Conservatives attribute poverty to character and policy not demography; Malthusian claims are not stated.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices filled by lottery contradicts Kirk's natural aristocracy and elections under the Constitution.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Goldwater defends free-market price setting and opposes government controls.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Goldwater treats the Constitution as a set of restraints, and the platform stresses civil liberties; the lean is against suspension.

party-controls-media.rationale: The platform opposes government censorship of lawful speech and Goldwater opposes state power over private life.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party-commanded army contradicts constitutional civilian command under the separation of powers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The platform's restriction emphasis suggests a stricter path to citizenship; this is inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives do not seek to cap representatives' pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Conservative parties accept caucus loyalty but Burkean tradition favours independent representatives; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Goldwater warns against surrendering sovereignty to the UN, and Wikipedia notes conservative scepticism of globalism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The American president commands the armed forces under the Constitution and conservatives defend a strong unitary executive, but the statement also includes choosing ministers, which fits the cabinet system.

church-by-bishops.rationale: American conservatism includes many denominations with different polities; there is no shared position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is never discussed; rejection is inferred from the constitutional republic conservatives defend, though the Christian right seeks religious influence.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Defeatism contradicts the patriotism and anti-communism central to the movement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Some social conservatives favour limits on obscenity but the movement values free speech, as the platform's stance shows.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Conservatives support the Twenty-second Amendment and limits on power; Kirk requires restraint of power.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; western conservatives have supported recalls while Burkeans prefer representation, so split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The platform keeps alliances while demanding allies pay, and paleoconservatives dissent, so the strands are split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory ownership contradicts property rights and freedom of contract.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun rights are supported but conservatives also demand a strong professional military, as the platform shows.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kirk's agrarian-leaning tradition and conservative geography favour rural life, but this is only a rough inference.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed; Goldwater's anti-communism supported Korea but the sources are silent.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The populist wing and Goldwater's school-quality critique hold that university-educated elites are out of touch, though the conservative intelligentsia also is university-educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order and civilisational emphasis, as well as Huntington, reject full cultural equivalence.

death-penalty.rationale: Conservatives and the platform's law-and-order stance generally support capital punishment, though some pro-life conservatives dissent.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The platform's Restore Parental Rights plank and social conservative stance oppose gender-focused curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Wikipedia notes conservatives question evolution more often, but the platform does not mention creationism and many conservatives prefer local control; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatives favour legal restrictions rooted in Kirk's moral order, although libertarian conservatives dissent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The platform wants to end chain migration but American conservatism accepts birthright citizenship traditionally, and the 14th Amendment question is debated; leaning against descent-only.

minority-language-support.rationale: The platform's emphasis on English and assimilation opposes public support for minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty and conservatives backed exemptions as in religious freedom laws.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Kirk's custom, convention and continuity principle values social conventions rather than prizing eccentricity, though freedom is also respected.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Conservatives favour repayment and oppose foreign aid, as Goldwater calls it ill-conceived.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives defend private property systems.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Goldwater and Kirk defend the existing constitution as inherited wisdom, so rewriting it by assembly is opposed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Goldwater ties political freedom to economic freedom, and he rejects trading one for the other.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Goldwater calls foreign aid ill-conceived and unconstitutional unless it serves national interests.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Goldwater supports American nuclear superiority and conservatives favour national deterrence, though this statement is about not relying on an ally, which is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Electoral College is defended by many conservatives but direct election has support too; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Mainstream fiscal conservatives favour price-stability-focused independent central banks, though the sources do not discuss it.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The platform stands with Israel but conservatives are split on territorial concessions; not directly addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater treat property as a basic right and foundation of freedom, not conditional on serving a common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Goldwater regards Soviet communism as a distinct mortal enemy; the state-capitalist thesis is not a conservative reading.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The platform rejects the Green New Deal and conservatives oppose acting on risks before scientific certainty when costs are high.

collective-defense.rationale: The 2024 platform asks allies to meet common-defence obligations, but recent conservatives make alliance support conditional, so strands differ.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Conservative anti-communism has treated Soviet-annexed Baltic states as occupied; this is inferred, not stated in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The platform promises to defend religious liberty and fight anti-Christian bias, the opposite of curbing the churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The American president is also a party leader and conservatives accept that; a ceremonial head of state is a parliamentary idea.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Conservatives venerate the Union and generally accept force to preserve it, though states' rights thinkers dissent.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Hong Kong-style arrangements are not discussed; conservatives favour uniform constitutional law.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred head of state is never discussed; rejection is inferred from conservatives' defence of the republican Constitution.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Goldwater argued that government may claim an equal percentage of each man's wealth, and conservatives often back flat taxes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Kirk holds that human nature is constant and Goldwater stresses individual responsibility, so character is not mainly circumstance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Goldwater treats the Constitution as a restraint on power and Kirk requires restraints, rejecting a ruler above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents are indifferent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Kirk's balanced power and variety principles and the Founders' mixed republic support mixing popular and elite elements.

leader-cult.rationale: Constitutional conservatism distrusts personality cults, although some populist supporters venerate leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; family-values conservatives are divided on custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine not addressed by conservatives, who reject socialism as such.

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking estates from owners violates the property right that Goldwater and Kirk defend.

refugee-return.rationale: The platform's restrictionist immigration stance points against large return rights; this is inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not discussed directly; mild disagreement is inferred from Goldwater's stress on national sovereignty and existing borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty under the First Amendment, so punishing apostasy is opposed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates are never discussed; rejection is inferred from the limited-government principles in Goldwater and the platform.

common-currency.rationale: Conservatives defend national sovereignty, and sceptics of the euro dominate, but the sources are silent.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cross-border political union of kin peoples is not an American conservative idea, so this is inferred from sovereignty emphasis.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; assimilationist emphasis implies conservatives disfavour separate institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; equal rights within the constitutional order is the conservative approach to minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order and Goldwater's priority of spiritual ends over material ones reject materialist history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is accepted in principle but modern conservatives are split about breaking up concentration.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-market conservatism opposes bailouts but government crisis action has often been accepted, so it is moderate.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional restraints limit what majorities may do, as Goldwater and Kirk hold, though conservatives also criticise activist judges.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandated gender representation contradicts the conservative stress on merit and opposes preferences.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The platform backs tariffs but not a closed bloc, and free-market conservatives favour trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Conservatives dislike binding labour and environmental standards, though tariff supporters favour conditions on trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Goldwater defends material incentives and individual responsibility, and Kirk rejects levelling.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guerrilla foco theory is never discussed; rejection is inferred from Kirk's prudence and Goldwater's constitutionalism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Kirk defends variety and inherited institutions, though American conservatives never had hereditary titles and the Constitution bans them.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The platform reinstates the 1776 Commission and Goldwater says schools transmit cultural heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Conservatives mostly reject imperial rule, though some neoconservatives are tolerant of tutelage; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The platform supports patriotic civics education and the 1776 Commission, and Goldwater says schools transmit cultural heritage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The platform would enforce civil rights law against race discrimination in schools, and conservatives broadly oppose affirmative action.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives defend the existing banking system and independent central banks.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Conservatives trust markets, but no cited source addresses whether capitalism avoids general crisis; mild agreement is inferred from Goldwater's market confidence.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed and adherents are indifferent.

delink-world-market.rationale: The platform seeks to expand American trade strength and energy exports, and conservatives reject delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Leninist labour-aristocracy thesis is never discussed; rejection is inferred from conservative defence of market gains for workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Goldwater held that private associations should be free but the platform opposes race discrimination; libertarians agree and social conservatives are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Goldwater holds that the Constitution limits government and Kirk requires restraints on power.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives favour treaty stability, though not formally argued.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republican tradition choosing rulers by election is accepted, in contrast to hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Individual veto over collective decisions is anarchist and contradicts constitutional rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Goldwater's constitutionalism and the American founding tradition accept resistance to rulers who violate the constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: American conservatives defend separated powers rather than legislative supremacy, so the statement does not map onto the American system.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Most conservatives accept animals' suffering matters while placing humans first; sources do not discuss.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Conservatives defend farming and research while accepting humane limits.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kirk valued inherited order and Goldwater preferred private charity, which suggests duties of the privileged, but neither states it; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater call for engaged citizens defending liberty, not withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School claim; conservatives criticise mass culture's moral effects but not as pacifying.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis; conservatives complain of cultural hegemony in media and academia, so partly agree.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Conservatives deny dependency theory, favouring free trade and local policy as causes of development.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Constitution already reserves the presidency for natural-born citizens, but other offices are open to naturalised citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist internal issue, not addressed by conservatives.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Goldwater says foreign aid is ill-conceived and stresses self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not American conservative; Goldwater stresses national interest more than revanchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Conservatives defend equal citizenship and oppose race-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Conservatives prefer anti-communism and the constitutional order as founding values; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Goldwater treats Communist threat as central, and anti-totalitarian conservatives condemn both.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Mainstream conservatives accept slavery caused the Civil War, though neo-Confederate strands dissent.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Kirk's continuity principle and heritage emphasis favour preserving monuments, and the 1776 Commission shows concern for national memory.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The platform's sports and family stances do not address this; sympathy exists on the conservative right but it is inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed and adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Paleoconservatives and Kirk's prescription favour tradition-bound forms while neoconservatives want to spread democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: American conservatives defend civilian control and constitutional separation of powers, not a political military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Conservatives favour family support through tax measures not state wages for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Familialism and enduring moral order support obligations to parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Chinese merit-exam model is foreign; conservatives rely on elections and patronage norms, though they admire merit.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The platform's America-first economic stance favours restrictions on foreign takeovers of strategic firms, though free-market conservatives disagree.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Social conservatives oppose no-fault divorce while the mainstream accepts it; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Kirk and Goldwater favour representation with independent judgment, not delegates removable at will.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour private accounts, though the 2024 platform promised no changes to Social Security.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only while used contradicts private property rights.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Congress's power of the purse is part of the separation of powers that conservatives defend.

single-official-language.rationale: The platform's English and assimilation emphasis and national conservatism support one common language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Recent conservative platforms back limits on foreign purchases of land, though property-rights conservatives disagree.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The platform's civil-rights focus on race discrimination and Goldwater's view of equal law reject discrimination by outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Kirk criticises materialism and Goldwater places spiritual ends first, while market conservatives defend consumption; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Goldwater's roll-back of communism and Reagan-era support to anti-communist insurgents show support, though paleoconservatives dissent.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not directly addressed; this is inferred from conservatives' support for self-determination of allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populist conservatives complain of corporate influence while the free-market wing defends political speech and donations; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The national-conservative strand wants limits on foreign influence, though the sources do not discuss this precisely.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Natalism is a listed conservative principle and the platform supports policies for families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Conservatives defend property rights, so local restrictions on buyers are disfavoured; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: A government job guarantee is the welfarism Goldwater opposes.

democratic-peace.rationale: Neoconservatives affirm the democratic peace, but paleoconservatives do not; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kirk stresses prescription and law, and Goldwater law and order, so there is a general duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Neoconservatives and Goldwater oppose absolute non-intervention while paleoconservatives support it.

industrial-unions.rationale: Goldwater attacks industry-wide bargaining power, but the structure of unions is not the movement's concern; indifferent.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream conservatives reject such conspiracy claims, though fringe voices exist.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The platform promotes the sanctity of marriage and familialism is a core principle.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Conservatives favour transparency in government in general but defend executive confidentiality; not discussed.

local-production.rationale: Market-oriented conservatives reject enforced localism while some agrarian traditionalists favour it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Conservatives work through parties, churches and elections rather than anarchist affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Goldwater warns against surrendering sovereignty to the UN and conservatives resist international courts.

religious-nation.rationale: The Christian right says the US was founded as a Christian nation, but the platform and most conservatives define the nation by constitutional citizenship; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute and ritual submission are inconsistent with American national interest and sovereignty.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Federalism favours local spending, but the sources are silent on regional revenue sharing.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal belongings being private is mainstream; Kirk's property principle covers all property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Goldwater states the aim is victory, not coexistence, and anti-communism united the movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Conservatives favour choice and competition in services, as the platform does in health, but this is inferred for publicly funded systems.

religion-illusion.rationale: Goldwater says man has spiritual needs and Kirk's first principle affirms moral order, so religion as an illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Goldwater credits markets for prosperity and Kirk defends property as the basis of civilisation, though Kirk also criticises materialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Conservatives reject the view that women's equality needs economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: The platform promotes support for families and the traditional family stance rejects public replacement of domestic care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a conservative concern in English; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Goldwater says only self-enforcing treaties are worth making and Congress's treaty power matters; not about internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Society reorganised into commons conflicts with property and constitutional order, though voluntary communities are valued by Kirk.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-directed settlement to alter demographics is opposed by constitutional conservatives.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: American conservatives embrace capitalism and oppose communism, so no third way is needed, though some traditionalists dissent.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Christian Zionists back historical claims but the sources do not discuss the principle; split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects Holocaust denial and the platform stands with Israel.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional conservatives once supported sodomy laws but most now accept their invalidation, with some still opposed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Goldwater's constitutional limits and the platform's free speech pledge oppose suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The First Amendment and the platform's religious liberty plank make blasphemy law unsupported by the movement.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not an American conservative position; Goldwater's aid views are not colonial.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal doctrine American conservatives never addressed; rejection is inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Overthrowing rulers by force for lacking religious law contradicts the constitutional order.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Conservatives favour representation and local voluntary community, not direct democracy in workplaces and universities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Conservatives reject intersectionality as a framework and the platform opposes critical race theory.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The platform opposes taxpayer funding for gender surgeries and rewriting Title IX, indicating opposition to legal recognition by gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: The pro-life and moral-order position leads most conservatives to oppose assisted dying, with some libertarian dissent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Goldwater and the movement define themselves against liberalism and the left, so the claim is rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist thesis that Goldwater and Kirk reject in defending wage work and property.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Some conservatives hold this while the mainstream distinguishes extremists; split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kirk's moral order and Goldwater's laws of God and nature place authority's source in God, though the Declaration roots government in consent too.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The platform defends religious liberty, so conservatives oppose restrictions on religious dress, notably in schools.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed and conservatives are split between contract freedom and protecting victims.

social-market-economy.rationale: Goldwater opposes welfarism and the movement favours markets with limited social protection, though Christian democratic forms exist.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Goldwater demands superiority and the platform wants the strongest military.

rich-first.rationale: Goldwater's defence of unequal outcomes from free markets and Kirk's variety principle support uneven growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Goldwater rejects neutrality toward communism and the platform stands with allies.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession of leaders is foreign to American republicanism, though Kirk values inherited institutions.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a conservative proposal; they defend private banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour austerity, so refusing lender conditions is disfavoured; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Kirk values property but the modern movement accepts universal suffrage, with some historical admirers.

domination-women-nature.rationale: A feminist-ecological claim that conservatives reject.

reification.rationale: A Marxist claim that conservatives reject.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Conservatives defend free press and private ownership and attack media bias instead.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Goldwater's constitutional limits and Kirk's rule of law, which the sources name as principle, favour standing laws applied by known judges.

racial-franchise.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects racial franchise limits and Goldwater affirms equal rights.

open-government-data.rationale: Conservatives broadly favour transparency but the sources are silent.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The platform's religious-liberty stance and civil-law approach oppose legal restrictions on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream conservatives condemn such discrimination as inconsistent with equal rights before law.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected assemblies conflict with Kirk's representative and prescriptive approach.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Kirk's respect for permanent moral truths and tradition resists reinterpretation by modern conditions, though liberal Protestants differ.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Goldwater regards concentrated power in government and unions as the danger, and Kirk defends property; the claim about wealth is not conservative.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The platform does not address it and conservative opinion has become divided.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Goldwater puts spiritual ends first and the platform defends religious liberty.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The platform promises to replenish police and lock up violent offenders.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Goldwater says charity should come from individuals, churches and local institutions rather than welfare programmes.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits were a conservative cause in the 1990s Contract with America, though not found in these sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed; conservatives prefer representation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed, and adherents are split on the priority of extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Many evangelical and Catholic conservatives restrict leadership offices by sex, though some denominations do not.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Evangelical complementarians and mainline conservatives differ on spousal authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The platform opposes voting rights for non-citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Goldwater defends free markets, which opposes price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Abolishing patents and copyrights contradicts property rights defended by Goldwater and Kirk.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Mainstream American conservatives favour patriotic education but not drilled mass youth movements, though the Boy Scouts are admired.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Goldwater wants American nuclear superiority and so opposes denying basing of nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The platform favours alliances and bases, but paleoconservatives dissent.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and conservatives are split on specific recognitions.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Goldwater and Kirk defend property returns as legitimate.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism contradicts the gun rights and strong defence the movement affirms.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Kirk values continuity but American conservatives do not assert ancient national origin; split.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The platform's sports and gender policies and Kirk's constant human nature reject this.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The platform's women's sports plank treats sex categories as fixed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring those who die for the nation is mainstream patriotism, though saints are not.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Goldwater frames spiritual ends above material and the religious right speaks of moral battle, but Kirk warns against ideological politics.

culture-before-state.rationale: Kirk's moral order stresses culture and Goldwater's constitutional politics stresses the state; split.

god-not-male.rationale: Most traditionalist conservatives keep traditional language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Conservatives reject judging scripture by a feminist standard, as Kirk holds moral truths are permanent.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Conservatives defend free enterprise open to all, not ethnic economic nationalism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; this is an irredentist idea that American conservatives do not hold.

independent-unions.rationale: Goldwater wanted voluntary unionism and opposed compulsory membership and union political power, which suggests agreement, but the sources do not address union independence from the state; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Conservatives reject socialism entirely so do not engage with its definition.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Conservatives favour private provision, though local public utilities are accepted.

second-chamber.rationale: The Senate and bicameralism embody Kirk's balanced power and the Constitution Goldwater defends.

municipal-property.rationale: Community ownership of the means of production contradicts private property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Kirk favours local decisions but conservatives defend the federal Constitution not confederal structures.

family-wage.rationale: Familialism and support for working parents suggest support for a wage that sustains a family, but it is not stated directly.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Free-market conservatives favour reducing regulatory delay, inferred from deregulation stance.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Government funding of life-extension research is not addressed; limited-government and pro-life views are split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Libertarian conservatives support financial privacy while law-and-order conservatives oppose untraceable payments; the sources are silent.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; free speech supporters favour it but others want identification.

person-over-state.rationale: Goldwater puts the individual first and Kirk places freedom and property above the state, though conservatives accept social duties.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Goldwater says man has spiritual as well as material needs and spiritual ends take priority, and Kirk's moral order concurs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Goldwater defends reserved state powers under the Tenth Amendment that Congress cannot withdraw.

gm-crops.rationale: Pro-market, pro-technology conservatives support biotech crops, but this is inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Conservatives favour suburbs and energy use, and rural life, and oppose density arguments.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mainstream conservatism rejects racial collectivism in favour of individual rights, though white identity strands exist.

racial-pride.rationale: Conservatives speak of national pride rather than racial pride; adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Goldwater's aim of victory over communism and neoconservative intervention depart from defensive-only use.

language-defines-nation.rationale: American nationhood is defined by creed and citizenship, not language alone.

communal-electorates.rationale: Religious separate electorates are never discussed; rejection is inferred from equal citizenship under the Constitution.

free-public-college.rationale: Conservatives oppose free tuition as a welfare entitlement, and the platform proposes closing the Department of Education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Conservatives oppose carbon and pollution taxes, though some economists on the right favour them.

future-generations.rationale: Kirk's idea of a partnership between the dead, the living and the unborn supports handing on resources, but conservatives dispute climate regulation.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Social conservatives hold complementary views but the sources do not present this political claim.

arms-reduction.rationale: Goldwater rejects parity and reductions and the platform demands the strongest military.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Goldwater stresses secure agreements and conservatives accept secret diplomacy for national security.

capital-controls.rationale: Conservatives favour free movement of capital as part of free markets.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The platform defends gun rights, so conservatives resist a state monopoly of arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Soldiers refusing orders contradicts the movement's military and patriotic stance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Goldwater opposes industry-wide bargaining and favours right-to-work, preferring individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Conservatives like the EITC as work-oriented but Goldwater opposed such redistribution; split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour balanced-budget rules, such as proposed amendments.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Goldwater calls foreign aid ill-conceived, and conservatives reject preferential restructuring.

smash-state-machine.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; Kirk and Goldwater defend the existing constitutional order.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Conservatives accept local variety but are not anarchic on economic systems; this is an anarchist idea.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Conservatives value property rights in resources but have not addressed pricing ecosystems.

sacred-nation.rationale: Patriotism is central and religious conservatives speak of providential mission, yet Kirk is wary of nation-worship; split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Conservatives oppose cancelling loans as an unfair, unconstitutional use of taxpayers' money.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Conservatives reject this as a left-wing framing.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kirk's first principle holds that human nature is constant, and moral truths permanent.

public-service-media.rationale: Conservatives distrust public media as biased, and the platform opposes government-backed content.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Conservative Christians hold Christianity true rather than all religions the same.

farm-price-support.rationale: Goldwater argues farm subsidies should end and the market control farm production.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Goldwater says superiority in nuclear arms is needed and parity will not do, so unilateral disarmament is rejected.

workers-own-party.rationale: Conservatives oppose class-based parties, though they court working-class voters.

ban-fgm.rationale: Conservatives broadly support prohibiting FGM as an assault on persons, though sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property rights fit conservative constitutionalism, but sources do not discuss it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Property rights principles support liability for harm to property, and conservatives prefer courts to regulation, though agencies also have defenders.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives favour the constitutional legislature, so an advisory chief role is disfavoured.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Goldwater puts liberty first and the platform ends restrictions on energy.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The platform's lock-up-violent-offenders stance and tough-on-crime conservatism support fixed sentences, though some conservatives favour judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: English-language assimilation is part of the platform's civics and assimilation emphasis.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Huntington-style arguments and national conservatives say diversity strains cohesion, while the mainstream and Goldwater's individualism stress shared creed over ethnicity; adherents are split.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power sharing is not discussed; American conservatives favour majority rule within constitutional limits, so this is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Goldwater backs right-to-work laws and voluntary unionism as central to limiting union power.

voter-id.rationale: The 2024 platform lists proof of citizenship, voter ID and paper ballots as core election-security measures.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from American conservatism's defence of religious liberty and limited government, which avoids state preference among interpretations, though it values religion in public life.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Conservatives stress the constitutional republic and its limits as well as elections, and the audit's sources do not settle this definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional moral order and support for marriage and family in Kirk's principles and the platform.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the platform's stress on free speech and limited government; shutdowns are not discussed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Mainstream conservatism, per Goldwater and the platform, keeps targeted programs with work requirements, though Friedmanite libertarians back a negative income tax.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not a live conservative dispute; inferred that adherents accept equal voting and office rights, as the Republican platform addresses women as voters and candidates.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Religion is central to the traditionalist core in Kirk's principles, and conservatives hold it supports family and women, not oppresses them.

race-social-construct.rationale: Mainstream conservatives are split between colour-blind individualism that treats race as socially built and those who reject the claim; the sources do not settle it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government principle in Goldwater, which opposes new federal bureaucracy for such goals.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's link between property and freedom and the Lockean tradition; the sources do not discuss original acquisition.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Goldwater and the platform stress national sovereignty and distrust supranational bodies, so adherents oppose trying American or allied leaders before international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the religious right reads scripture literally while traditionalist, libertarian and secular strands do not, so adherents are split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: conservatives value group self-rule and women's equality alike but rarely address how the two combine in group self-government, and strands differ.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Goldwater's call to defeat rather than coexist with communism makes defending a communist planned state against restoration contrary to the movement.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of the Electoral College and the Founders' mixed system; it does not otherwise favour council-based delegate selection.

national-church-status.rationale: American conservatives champion religious liberty and the First Amendment's ban on establishment, so a legally privileged national church is not their position despite their emphasis on religion.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's preference for equal treatment and constitutional uniformity; it supports states' rights and tribal sovereignty but not ethnic territorial autonomy as such.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's emphasis on self-government and Cold War support for self-determination; the sources do not address plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's respect for prescription and established order, which favours inherited arrangements over redrawing borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the movement celebrates free enterprise, prosperity and abundance, though Kirk values prudence and variety, so limiting needs is not an ideal it holds.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to property rights, free movement within the country and opposition to federal land-use restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the conservative majority and religious right resist drafting women, though some conservatives accept equal registration, so confidence is low.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Kirk's emphasis on custom, continuity and patriotism suggests agreement, but the sources do not state a spiritual-bond-with-land position; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Goldwater's constitutionalism and the platform's law-and-order stress operate within due process, and mainstream conservatives reject killing suspects without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: The 2024 platform treats China as a strategic rival and seeks to cut dependence on it, which is the opposite of seeking close ties.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: American conservatism emphasises national interest and sovereignty and has no tradition of state support for kin abroad; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The movement's defence of private property and free enterprise rejects equal common ownership of resources and compensation to all.

self-ownership.rationale: Libertarian and fusionist strands endorse strong individual rights over body and labour, though traditionalists qualify it; inferred from the movement's liberty emphasis.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The platform's low-tax stance favours tax cuts generally, but conservatives often prefer consumption taxes to income taxes, so a specific cut is an inference.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Conservatives favour means-tested aid and limited government over universal programmes, but the sources do not address this directly; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Kirk's principles stress intermediate institutions and restraints on power, and Goldwater defends constitutional checks, rejecting rule that bypasses parties and groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Free-enterprise rhetoric opposes special privileges, though Republican policy often favours particular industries; inferred and contested.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The religious right is a major faction and the platform draws on religious values, so most adherents reject excluding religion from politics, though not denominational organisation as such; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Kirk's defence of tradition alongside a modern commercial order suggests agreement, but the sources do not state this; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: No-fault divorce is legal everywhere in the US and rarely a conservative target, though some social conservatives oppose it; inferred and contested.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 2024 platform stresses American energy and resource independence and reducing reliance on foreign sources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Its stress on property, free enterprise and limited government treats fair acquisition and liberty as more important than equality of outcome; inferred from those principles.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement's low-tax, free-market stance opposes new levies on financial markets; inferred, as the sources do not name such a tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Mainstream conservatives, and the 2024 platform's stand against race-based preferences, hold that colour-blind policy and family and culture now matter more than racism; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Kirk's belief in a transcendent moral order favours natural law, while the movement's constitutionalism stresses obedience to lawful procedure; adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The sources take no stand on automation; conservatives prize work and enterprise but also free-market technological change, so adherents are split.

multipolar-world.rationale: The platform and Goldwater's anti-communism favour American strength and leadership rather than a balance of independent powers, though national conservatives lean toward restraint; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The movement's free-market economics holds that value comes from markets, capital and enterprise as well as labour; inferred from its defence of free enterprise.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Patriotism is central to the movement and its populist and national-conservative wing courts working people, but the traditional wing opposes worker-focused politics; adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Conservatives oppose identity politics and the 2024 platform stresses jobs, wages and prices, so they would agree the left should focus on material interests; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement is anti-communist and holds that socialism and one-party rule contradict freedom and free markets; inferred from that stance.

missingStatements.text: Workers should not be required to join or pay a union as a condition of employment.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldwater backs right-to-work laws and voluntary unionism as central to limiting union power.

missingStatements.text: Government should have only the powers specifically delegated to it by a written constitution, with all others left to the states and the people.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldwater treats the Tenth Amendment as a binding rule and the Constitution as a system of restraints; Kirk stresses restraints on power.

missingStatements.text: Voters should have to show proof of citizenship and identification to vote.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2024 platform lists proof of citizenship, voter ID and paper ballots as core election-security measures.

notes: Strands differ: libertarian-leaning conservatives dissent on drugs, surveillance and immigration; national conservatives on trade and entitlements; neoconservatives on intervention; paleoconservatives on foreign policy. The profile follows the mainstream Republican-aligned centre as of 2024.
